title: SecPaging: Secure Enclave Paging with Hardware-Enforced Protection against Controlled-Channel Attacks
problem: Trusted Execution Environments like Intel SGX are vulnerable to controlled-channel attacks where untrusted operating systems manipulate page tables or observe page faults to deduce enclave secrets.
motivation: TEEs are widely adopted for privacy-preserving computing, but current paging mechanisms lack sufficient hardware-level protection against controlled-channel attacks that can leak sensitive enclave data.
method: SecPaging employs hardware-enforced and microcode-supported protection mechanisms: enclave page table entries are protected through hardware isolation preventing privileged tampering, an Eager-Allocation mechanism pre-allocates pages to prevent allocation-based attacks, and a Record-Reload mechanism tracks page swaps to prevent swap-based attacks. The implementation is evaluated on real SGX hardware.
key_novelty: Hardware-enforced isolation of enclave page tables combined with Eager-Allocation and Record-Reload mechanisms to jointly defend against both allocation-based and swap-based controlled-channel attacks.
contributions: Hardware isolation mechanism for protecting enclave page table entries against privileged OS tampering
Eager-Allocation technique to prevent allocation-based controlled-channel attacks
Record-Reload mechanism to prevent swap-based controlled-channel attacks
Prototype implementation and evaluation on SGX with minimal performance overhead
primary_theme: secure enclave paging against controlled-channel attacks
